sw19b.name: We are operating on about one-sixteenth, fixed for sense: what the sixteenth counts, what the Void is, what to do
sw19b.text: That works out to about one-sixteenth of the grown-ups per child that our brains evolved with (Perry, 2023). So the empty feeling you may carry, the "Void" this guide keeps coming back to, is real: it's what that missing company feels like. Once you've de-armored, going back to a lonely life will feel worse than it did with the armor on. Gather a tribe around you, people you're close to and see most days, or your brain will eventually reach for the armor again just to survive the cold.

sw22b.name: The Anti-Breakthrough, fixed for sense: the window first, then the hour, then the act
sw22b.text: The Anti-Breakthrough (Micro-Dosing): A brain stuck in alarm can often take in healing work for only a few seconds at a time, Dr. Perry finds. So for now we have to give up on the hour-long breakthrough that therapy aims for, since an hour spent working on the trauma itself overwhelms an armored nervous system more than it heals it. Instead, this protocol works in doses of a few seconds, and those small doses are what I mean by micro-dosing here.

sw22-23b.name: The Anti-Breakthrough with the practice after it (41 words), both fixed for sense
sw22-23b.text:
The Anti-Breakthrough (Micro-Dosing): A brain stuck in alarm can often take in healing work for only a few seconds at a time, Dr. Perry finds. So for now we have to give up on the hour-long breakthrough that therapy aims for, since an hour spent working on the trauma itself overwhelms an armored nervous system more than it heals it. Instead, this protocol works in doses of a few seconds, and those small doses are what I mean by micro-dosing here.

Your goal is small doses of feeling safe in your body: 30 seconds of slow, steady breathing, twenty times a day. It works the way physical therapy rebuilds an injured knee, where many short sessions do more than a long one.
